author: Katie Kaplan
title: Former Madison County Treasurer's trial set for Sept.; Plea deal possible - NewsBreak
text:
By Katie Kaplan No media credit provided. ,
1 days ago
WINTERSET, Iowa (WHO) — The upcoming criminal trial for former Madison County Treasurer Amanda DeVos is set to proceed despite a plea deal on the table.
During a pretrial hearing on Monday morning, prosecutors stated that a plea offer had been “tendered” to DeVos, who has pleaded not guilty. Her attorney indicated that they were reviewing the offer but had not accepted the terms.
The upcoming trial against embattled Madison County Treasurer Amanda DeVos, 37, has been moved to Boone County. In the meantime, the Sept. 1 trial is progressing as planned. It will take place in Boone County after a change of venue was granted last May. It is expected to last three days. Roughly 40 jurors will be summoned for the case.
DeVos was elected to a four-year term in November 2022 and began serving that term on Jan. 1, 2023, before her arrest in January of 2025 for allegedly using her access as county treasurer to alter government records. In October of 2024, she allegedly changed a county database to make it look like she had paid nearly $800 for her vehicle registration. She was charged with Felonious Misconduct in Office (class D felony), Tampering with Records (aggravated misdemeanor), Fraudulent Practices in the third degree (aggravated misdemeanor) and third-degree Theft (aggravated misdemeanor).
Weeks later, WHO 13 was the first to report that she was under investigation for an entirely different criminal scenario, allegedly involving her property taxes.
Former Madison County Treasurer Amanda DeVos faces multiple felonies. Nine months later in December, DeVos was charged with a second count of Felonious Misconduct in Office, as well as Fraudulent Practices in the Second Degree. Court records allege that the new charges stemmed from May of 2024, when DeVos knowingly altered records related to her property taxes in an amount between $1,500 and $10,000.
Story continues below
Public property tax records show she and her husband purchased their home in Winterset’s Copper Fox Estates in 2018 for $375,000. The taxes owed for that property for July 1, 2023, through June 30, 2024, were $5,830.00, according to a county tax bill that also boasts DeVos’ official Treasurer letterhead.
DeVos has not been charged in connection with the apparent mishandling of county funds, which appears to have plagued nearly every municipality and school district in Madison County under her tenure.
The Madison County Courthouse. 2025 WHO 13 also previously discovered that the City of Winterset received more than $250,000 in funds meant for other municipalities and confirmed that late property tax payments to the Winterset Community School District forced it to withdraw funds from investment opportunities to cover payroll.
Other local governments and organizations that confirmed to WHO 13 in early 2025 that they had an issue with either late payments, overpayments, double payments, erroneous deposits, and/or communication with the treasurer’s office included the following:
The community of Earlham The City of Macksburg The City of Patterson The City of St. Charles The City of Truro Earlham Community Schools The Interstate 35 Community School District DeVos had allegedly refused to resign from her elected position and had continued collecting her county-issued paycheck and benefits, which then forced the county attorney to file a Ch. 66 petition to have her forcefully removed from office. She officially resigned in mid-July, without admitting any wrongdoing.
